# ebook2cw

**Converts a text file or ebook into Morse code audio at a chosen speed**

- **Version recorded:** 0.8.5
- **Categories:** `cw`, `morse-training`
- **Upstream:** <https://fkurz.net/ham/ebook2cw.html>

## What it does

Reads plain text and writes it out as Morse audio in MP3 or Ogg Vorbis, splitting a long book into one file per chapter. Speed, Farnsworth spacing, sidetone pitch and effective word rate are all set on the command line, and the ID3 tags carry the chapter titles so a player treats the result like an audiobook.

## Why you would want it

Head copy is a listening skill and it improves with hours, not with exercises. This turns any text you already want to read into those hours on a phone or a car stereo, at exactly the speed you are currently failing at. It is the practical answer to "I do not have time to practise".

## Before it will work

None. It writes files; it does not touch a sound card or a radio.

## Install and launch

- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## How it installs

- apt: `ebook2cw`

## Known problems

The default 25 wpm is faster than most people expect. Set the effective speed with -e well below the character speed set with -w — that is Farnsworth spacing, and learning at full character speed with long gaps is the method that works. Starting at a low character speed is the mistake it makes easy.
